newsitem.title: USA: Junk to supply bulk of US new corp issues this wk.
newsitem.headline: Junk to supply bulk of US new corp issues this wk.

text.p: This week's bulk of new issue action will be brought by junk bond issuers who are slated to bring about $2.2 billion in new supply as more interest rate sensitive high-grade issuers take to the sidelines, dealers said.
"Right now most business is slated to come from the junk sector," said one dealer. "If rates come back down a bit we may see some investment grade offerings but for now that sector's very quiet."
Currently, the benchmark 30-year bond is trading up 4/32 at 97-28/32 to yield 6.54 percent.

With the yield on the 30-year bond back above 6.50 percent, issuance in the investment-grade arena is expected to remain on hold as financing debt turns more expensive for the more higher-rated credits.
Just two and a half weeks ago, on July 30, the long bond was yielding 6.30 percent at the close, its lowest level in over a year.
The Federal Reserve Board's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday but market participants expect no further tightening in U.S. monetary policy.

Meanwhile, among this week's batch of new junk bond offerings is Southern Foods Group $150 million in 10-year 144a senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities. Price talk on the issue is seen between 325-350 basis points, syndicate sources said.
Golden Ocean Group is slated to bring a $150 million four-year 144a senior subordinated note offering, sources said.
Later in the week, Murrin Murrin Holdings will issue a $400 million two-part debt offering via Natwest Capital Markets, sources said.
